payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Astrid, Gillian, Reanna

payload.content: Hi team! I've analyzed the tasks and my costs. The ISSUE-0002 security tasks are a great fit for my skills (ui-ux-design: 0.87, security: 0.71) with low costs - implement: 2.24, review: 1.12, test: 1.57. The ISSUE-0001 api-development tasks have very high costs for me (60-42) since they don't match my skillset. I'm happy to take any of the ISSUE-0002 tasks, particularly the review or test tasks given my availability of 7 hours. What are your preferences?

From a team optimization perspective: ISSUE-0001 tasks are critical priority but have very high costs for me (60 for implement, 42 for test, 30 for review/docs/triage). ISSUE-0002 tasks are medium priority but much more efficient for me given my skill match. I suggest someone with api-development skills should take ISSUE-0001 tasks while I focus on ISSUE-0002. I'm flexible on which ISSUE-0002 task to take - all fit within my 7-hour availability.

Hi Gillian! Thanks for sharing your analysis. I have strong api-development skills (0.98) which makes ISSUE-0001 tasks much more efficient for me. My costs are significantly lower than yours for the critical priority tasks: ISSUE-0001::triage=2.22, review=2.78, docs=2.78, test=3.89, implement=5.55. Since you prefer ISSUE-0002 tasks and I can handle ISSUE-0001 efficiently, how about I focus on ISSUE-0001 (probably triage or review) while you take one of the ISSUE-0002 tasks? This would maximize team efficiency. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Hi Gillian and Reanna! Thanks for sharing your analyses. I have UI-UX-design skills (0.72) but no api-development skills. My costs for ISSUE-0001 tasks are very high (24-60) due to skill mismatch, while ISSUE-0002 tasks are much more reasonable: implement=4.34, review=2.17, test=3.04. With 6 hours availability, I can efficiently handle any ISSUE-0002 task. Since Reanna is well-suited for ISSUE-0001 and Gillian prefers ISSUE-0002, how about I take the ISSUE-0002::test task? This leaves implement and review for Gillian/Harry coordination. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Sounds like we have a solid plan! Reanna takes ISSUE-0001 (critical tasks), Astrid takes ISSUE-0002::test, and I'll take ISSUE-0002::review. This leaves ISSUE-0002::implement available for Harry if he's participating, or we can adjust if needed. The review task is perfect for me - only 1 hour effort, lowest cost (1.12), and excellent skill match. Ready to commit to ISSUE-0002::review during execution phase. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Team, just confirming our coordination: I'm planning to take ISSUE-0001::triage (critical priority, good skill match for me). This aligns with our earlier discussion about specialization. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Confirming our coordination: I'll take ISSUE-0002::test as planned. Reanna takes ISSUE-0001::triage, Gillian takes ISSUE-0002::review, and Harry takes ISSUE-0002::implement. This gives us optimal task distribution with good skill matches and low costs across the board. Ready for execution phase!

Final confirmation before execution: Our plan looks solid! I (Gillian) will take ISSUE-0002::review (1hr, cost 1.12) - perfect fit for my skills and availability. Reanna takes ISSUE-0001::triage (critical priority, her expertise), Astrid takes ISSUE-0002::test, and Harry takes ISSUE-0002::implement. This covers 4 tasks total with optimal skill matching and minimal costs. Ready to commit during execution phase!

Final coordination check: Ready to commit to ISSUE-0002::review during execution phase. This gives us 4 tasks covered with optimal skill matching. Reanna on ISSUE-0001::triage (critical), me on ISSUE-0002::review, Astrid on ISSUE-0002::test, Harry on ISSUE-0002::implement. Let's stick to the plan!

Final confirmation before execution: I'm taking ISSUE-0001::triage (critical priority, 2.22 cost, good skill match). This aligns with our team optimization plan. Ready to commit! (phase=planning, iter=1)

Team, there's a coordination issue: both Gillian (on blackboard 0) and Stefania (mentioned by Harry on blackboard 3) are planning to take ISSUE-0002::review. We need to clarify who will actually take this task to avoid duplication. Can someone confirm Stefania's actual assignment? Otherwise we risk a violation penalty. I remain committed to ISSUE-0002::test as planned.

Team update on coordination: Our coalition (Mi and I) have finalized our assignments. I'm taking ISSUE-0001::triage (critical priority) and Mi is taking ISSUE-0002::test. This leaves ISSUE-0002::review available for Stefania if she's participating, avoiding any duplication conflicts with Gillian. This gives us optimal task coverage across both critical and medium priority tasks.

Team update: The ISSUE-0002::review conflict appears resolved - Reanna mentioned Mi is taking ISSUE-0002::test (not review), which leaves ISSUE-0002::review available. Based on blackboard 3 coordination, Stefania should take ISSUE-0002::review, Gillian should find an alternative. I'm still committed to ISSUE-0002::test. Can someone confirm final assignments for execution phase? (phase=planning, iter=1)
